summary: US-P3: Early-bird tiers switch over by the clock alone — no manual intervention
description:
**As** an organizer, **I want** to schedule an early-bird price and its successors up front, **so that** the price changes on time without anyone being awake for it.

**Priority:** P0  **Depends on:** TKT-151 (hierarchy + provenance exist)

TKT-5's second COS: *scheduled price changes (early-bird tiers) apply without manual intervention*. The lazy correct reading of 'without manual intervention' is **no scheduler at all** — a rule carries an effective window and resolution is evaluated against request time, so the tier flips by the passage of time and nothing has to run. If the plan proposes a cron/job instead, it must argue why evaluation-time windowing is insufficient.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A price rule carries an effective window; both bounds nullable (unbounded). The interval is **half-open `[starts_at, ends_at)`** and that is stated in the OpenAPI description — an inclusive/exclusive ambiguity at a tier boundary is a real money bug.
- [ ] Resolution filters by the caller-supplied evaluation instant (defaulting to now), so **no scheduled job, cron, or write is required** for a tier to take effect. A test proves it: from one fixed dataset with **no write in between**, resolving at `ends_at - 1ns` yields the early-bird tier and at `ends_at` yields the next one.
- [ ] Overlapping windows at the same scope level resolve deterministically by a documented rule (e.g. narrower window wins, then the TKT-151 tie-break) — proven by a test with two deliberately overlapping tiers.
- [ ] Provenance names the **active tier** as well as the winning scope level, and reports the tier that lost on time (not just the ones that lost on scope).
- [ ] An expired or not-yet-started rule is invisible to resolution and never leaks into provenance as a winner; with all tiers expired, resolution falls back exactly as TKT-151 specified (no-rule → ticket type's base price).
- [ ] The window filter is **index-backed** per ADR-019 (result scoped *and* scan scoped); plain `CREATE INDEX` (ADR-020). OpenAPI regenerated and committed before the gate; the operation stays covered in catalog's own coverage test (ADR-030).
- [ ] The ADR-004 TTL tier is **re-argued**, not inherited: a response whose correctness expires at a known instant cannot be cached past that instant. State how the declared TTL interacts with a tier boundary.

Quality gates: `make check` green (lint + unit + integration, mirrors CI); contract tests for any touched service boundary (OpenAPI drift check, ADR-009); public-read stories declare their ADR-004 TTL tier with rationale; entities `organizer_id`-scoped (ADR-002); money is integer minor units + ISO-4217 code, floats banned (ADR-001).

objective.note: Early-bird pricing is table stakes; doing it by hand at midnight is the failure mode this removes.

scope.note: IN: effective windows on rules, evaluation-time filtering, overlap semantics, provenance of the active tier, TTL interaction. OUT: quantity-tiered / demand-based pricing, channel windows (TKT-17), commerce wiring (TKT-153).

uncertainties.note: Overlap tie-break (narrowest-window vs latest-start) is a design call resolvable in Planning against TKT-150's conflict semantics; it does not need a product decision.

approach.note: Extend TKT-151's rule table with the window columns and thread an evaluation instant through the same pure resolver — same test seam, table-driven with fixed instants (no wall-clock in tests).

first_slice.note: Windows on the existing rule shape; demoable by resolving the same data at two instants and getting two prices.

success.note: COS-2 of TKT-5, proven by the no-write-in-between boundary test.

context_memo.note: Baked below; governingAdrs resolved from docs/adr/ at 2026-07-30 and to be re-resolved at claim time.

binding.rule: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code — floats are banned on money paths.
Pin time-sensitive assertions to the DB's clock, not the test process's, so the boundary under test is the only moving part.

governingAdrs.why: Money on every pricing path is integer minor units + ISO-4217 code; a percentage/discount rule must not introduce a float or a rounding-by-float step.

Catalog owns **rule definitions**; commerce owns **pricing evaluation at sale time**. Do not put rule CRUD in commerce, and do not put cart/fee/promo evaluation in catalog (docs/architecture.md service table).
Contract-first: the OpenAPI document is the source of truth, regenerate `openapi_gen.go` / `api-types.gen.ts` and commit them BEFORE running the gate (check-generate diffs against HEAD).

Migrations run out-of-band via the binary's `migrate` subcommand as a one-shot Compose job; the server path never migrates. New migration files follow the existing numbering in `services/<svc>/internal/store/migrations/`.
Any public read this story adds declares a volatility TTL tier with rationale. A resolved price is availability-adjacent, not seat-map-stable — argue the tier, don't copy one.
A scoped read is only scoped if an index backs the filter. Proving it takes TWO tests: the result is scoped *and* the scan is (plan assertion, not just output).
Plain `CREATE INDEX` — `CONCURRENTLY` is still NOT adopted; preconditions (2) and (3) remain false even after ADR-022. Do not 'improve' this.

Catalog is deliberately OUT of the smoke happy-path coverage gate; its per-operation coverage gate is `services/catalog/internal/api/coverage_test.go`. A new catalog operation must be exercised THERE, not in the smoke suite.
Series/season grouping is the hierarchy level between venue and event — reuse the existing `series`/`seasons` shape, don't invent a parallel grouping.
Sharpened for this ticket: a resolved price with a known expiry instant must not be cacheable past it. The TTL tier is a correctness argument here, not a performance one.

reference.summary: TKT-134's learning — pin the hold by DB time so release is the test's only moving boundary — is the closest precedent for testing a time boundary in this repo.
The existing operating-window columns on `performances` (migration 0004) show the repo's convention for representable time bounds.
